drafted_from: tool:github:microsoft-markitdown's row in tools/tools-from-github/tool-rows.json (job, run, get_it, needs) and its sources row in sources.json; the command is the row's own run line with synthetic names filled in. What it prints or writes is read from the tool's documented behavior; the folder test test/index-github-tools.test.mjs only checks the row, never runs markitdown.
start_here: Say to your AI: "Use markitdown on my computer to turn a PDF: the file is menu.pdf." It reads the row, installs markitdown if it is missing, runs it on that one file and shows you what it made.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: markitdown is a program that runs on the person's own computer and works on the one file or address it is handed.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Use markitdown on menu.pdf". It reads the row with run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools, method tools:list, input {tool: "tool:github:microsoft-markitdown"}.
2. It checks that python are on your computer, and if markitdown is missing it runs the get_it steps: git clone https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown.git ; pip install 'markitdown[all]'.
3. It runs the row's command with your file in place of {input} and where the result goes in place of {output}: markitdown menu.pdf -o menu.md
4. Read what it shows you and open the result. Trillion runs none of this; it all happens on your own computer.

worked_examples.title: markitdown on a one page PDF menu of a bakery
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/tools-from-github/tool-rows.json: tool:github:microsoft-markitdown runs on your computer, so after tools:list the AI runs, in the folder it got markitdown in, the command line: markitdown menu.pdf -o menu.md  (synthetic input: a one page PDF menu of a bakery).
worked_examples.hands_back: markitdown writes menu.md: the text of menu.pdf as Markdown, with headings as "#" lines and each price list as "-" lines.
